title: Verdict-to-audit mapping: each enforcement outcome lands on the right execution status
risk: Operators and auditors cannot tell whether an action was executed, refused or is waiting, so dashboards and post-incident reviews draw the wrong conclusion.
preconditions: Namespace gov-unit-auth-<case_id>-<worker_id>; no shared mutable state with other cases.
PolicyEnforcementPoint loaded with fixtures/offline/governance.json skill_authority_registry and agents[]; clock frozen at 2026-01-15T10:00:00Z.

steps.action: Submit the four probes and collect the four verdicts
steps.expected: Verdicts are PERMIT, DENY_PROHIBITED, REQUIRE_HUMAN_APPROVAL and LIMIT_EXCEEDED respectively.
execution_status values are success, denied, denied, denied; APPROVAL-PENDING is represented as denied plus an approval reference, never as success.

steps.action: Force a connector failure and an unknown-outcome timeout in two extra probes
steps.expected: Failure maps to failed and unknown outcome maps to pending or a dedicated reconciliation state, never to success.

assertions: Every verdict maps to exactly one execution_status and the mapping is total over the six outcomes.
No probe produces success when it was not permitted and externally executed.
REQUIRE_HUMAN_APPROVAL rows carry an approval ticket reference so the pause is traceable.
The six mapping entries are enforceable as data, not hardcoded in the assertion (changing the fixture changes the expectation).
forbidden: Mapping an unknown outcome to success because the request returned 200.
Collapsing denial and approval-pending into one status.
Writing a success row for a probe that never reached a connector.
evidence: Verdict JSON and audit row pairs for all six probes.
Connector call log showing which probes actually dispatched.
cleanup: Delete gov- run rows after exporting the mapping table.
automation: Real PEP verdict emission, audit mapping and reconciliation state machine under test; connector behaviour is substituted with an injectable failure/timeout stub. Deterministic clock drives the timeout.
